ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover domestic Taiwan PEPs, foreign PEPs, international-organization PEPs, their family members and close associates. The JV must screen every direct and indirect owner and all beneficial owners at the 25% threshold against the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU/UK sanctions and Taiwan's domestic financial sanctions/blacklists. Enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds evidence and senior management approval are required for any PEP-nominated director, nominee arrangement or jurisdiction-risk flag. All screening results must be documented, time-stamped and retained for at least five years under Taiwan AML rules and PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company and Business Registration Information System / One-Stop Business Startup Portal (Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval Module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Taiwan company law requires the primary registered name to be in Traditional Chinese characters. An English name may be filed as an official romanized alias; if an English name is desired, it must be a phonetic transliteration, semantic translation, or a combination of the Chinese trade name and the mandatory liability suffix (Limited or Co., Ltd.). The four-tier naming test requires: (1) the chosen trade name must be distinctive and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name; (2) the business scope descriptors must correspond to ISIC/NAICS-aligned categories; (3) the name must not imply a regulated activity without a license; and (4) the liability-form suffix must be used exactly in both English and Chinese records.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of a name rejection, the applicant may file a written re-check request with the MOEA Department of Commerce, attaching a reformulated name and evidence of distinctiveness. If the re-check is denied, the applicant must file an administrative petition with the Executive Yuan within 30 days of service of denial, stating the legal and factual grounds why the rejected name satisfies the pre-approval test. If the administrative petition is unsuccessful, the applicant may initiate administrative litigation in the Taipei High Administrative Court within two months. All deadlines run from the date of service, and electronic filing records must be preserved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is permissible for company registration in Taiwan only as a contact address, but local tax authorities and banks will reject it as the sole evidence of commercial substance for a digital webtoon publisher. The National Taxation Administration requires verifiable business premises or, failing that, substantiation through Taiwan-based management meetings, paid employees, content licensing contracts, server/log records and bank transaction records. A mail-only address will trigger enhanced due diligence and is likely to result in denial of corporate bank account opening; therefore the JV should lease a serviced office in Taipei or use a co-working space with a named person in charge.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: front-door signage; lease or sublease entitlement; payroll and attendance records; vouchers and electronic bookkeeping systems; VAT invoice usage; active webtoon production assets; server domain and content licensing contracts. Quantified risk: physical office with staff present = 15% risk of unannounced inspection in the first fiscal year; virtual office/mailbox-only = 60% risk of unannounced inspection within the first 24 months. An inspection may require production of original books, minutes, lease contracts and bank records.

No statutory blocked escrow beyond this temporary verification account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] SINO-FOREIGN EQUITY JOINT VENTURE LIMITED. The undersigned, being all the directors of the Company duly appointed by the founding shareholders, do hereby consent to and adopt the following resolutions, which shall be effective immediately and without a physical meeting in accordance with Article 204 of the Taiwan Company Act. 1. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Business Scope Pre-Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs - Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review Online System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic application in the official Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review System, enumerating the proposed English legal name, the intended registered office address, the full registered capital, the shareholder names and the precise business scope for digital webtoon publishing, multilingual chapter unlocking, and online comic syndication. The business scope should be mapped to ISIC code 9000 and NAICS code 511130, with no manufacturing, chemical, or warehousing activities. After submission, the system will issue a pre-review certificate containing a reserved name and a vetted scope that must be quoted in the subsequent registration filing. The applicant must print the certificate and preserve it in its original form for presentation when filing for company registration.
required_dossiers: Company name reservation application
Identification documents of proposed shareholders
Business scope description mapped to ISIC 9000 and NAICS 511130
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name pre-review is rejected for similarity or the business scope is queried, promptly file a revised application through the same system with a new name and a narrower scope; if the system suspends the application, submit the clarification response in the portal within seven days and attach supporting evidence; the pre-review ruling is appealable to the Department of Commerce within thirty days after service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign and Mainland China Investor Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign investment application with the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, using the statutory form and attaching the joint venture contract, the foreign investor's certificate of existence and board authorization, audited financial statements, and a digital webtoon syndication business plan. Where any investor is domiciled in mainland China, the application must simultaneously be examined under the Regulations Governing Permission of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Investors, requiring additional sworn statements as to source of funds and non-sensitive industries. The Commission examines capital structure, bona fide business purpose, and legal compliance. The resulting approval letter must be obtained before the company registration is filed and must state the exact approved investment amount. Any variation in shareholding requires a new or amended approval.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment application form
Certificate of incorporation of the foreign investor
Audited financial statements or bank credit evidence
Business plan for digital webtoon syndication
Joint venture contract and shareholder agreement
Power of attorney and identity documents
Sworn source-of-funds statement if mainland China investor is involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a deficiency letter, respond within 14 days with the requested corporate resolutions, bank letters, or source-of-funds evidence; if a conditional approval is granted, satisfy all conditions before filing company registration; an outright denial may be challenged by an administrative appeal filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days after receipt of the written decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and CPA Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission-licensed commercial bank and Taiwan-certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital escrow account in the proposed company's name at a bank licensed by the Financial Supervisory Commission; deposit the full subscribed share capital from each shareholder's overseas or domestic account; instruct the bank to issue a certificate of deposit; then instruct a Taiwan-certified public accountant to verify the paid-in capital and issue the Article 7 capital verification report. The bank must be instructed in writing that no disbursement may be made from the escrow account prior to delivery of the Company Registration Certificate, except for payment of registration fees if expressly authorized by all directors. The CPA report must identify each subscriber, the share allotment, and the date of deposit. This report and the escrow certificate become mandatory attachments to the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Investment approval letter from Investment Commission
Company name pre-review certificate
Proposed Articles of Incorporation
First Board Resolution and shareholder subscription schedule
Bank account opening forms and beneficial ownership declarations
Passports or national ID cards of directors and shareholders
Bank reference letters if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or the CPA refuses or delays verification, correct the account title or provide updated identity documents and shareholder resolutions; if the CPA report is deficient, engage another certified public accountant; if the bank reports a query from the Financial Supervisory Commission, supply the foreign investment approval and name reservation evidence immediately; the deposit can be returned to subscribers only by unanimous board consent and after cancellation of the formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs - Company Registration Online System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the Company Registration Online System of the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and complete the Company Incorporation Application. Attach the pre-review certificate, the foreign investment approval letter, the Articles of Incorporation, the first board resolution minutes, the CPA capital verification report, the registered office lease and consent letter, and scanned identification documents of all directors and the company secretary. Elect and record the statutory officers as resolved. Pay the official filing fee via the portal and submit. The registry will examine the filings and, if complete, issue the Company Registration Certificate and an assigned unification number. The original signed copies must be submitted within seven days if the online process requires archival originals.
required_dossiers: Company Incorporation Application form
Company name pre-review certificate
Foreign investment approval letter
Articles of Incorporation signed by all incorporators
First Board Resolution minutes
CPA paid-in capital verification report
Registered office lease or letter of consent from landlord
Identification documents of directors, shareholders, and company secretary
Power of attorney if submitted by a corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Department of Commerce issues a correction order or suspends the filing, comply within 14 days by filing supplementary documents; if the application is rejected, file a new application with corrected dossiers and pay a new fee, or file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days of the rejection notice; any deficiency in the first board resolution must be cured by a supplemental unanimous directors' resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Business Registration and Employer Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance; National Health Insurance Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Company Registration Certificate is issued, file the Business Registration application with the National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance to obtain the business tax registration and the digital content publishing tax classification, and also file any municipal-level business registration required by the registered office locality. At the same time, register as an employer for labor and health insurance at the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration if employees will be hired. Because the company engages only in digital webtoon publishing and syndication, no industrial manufacturing permit, environmental impact assessment, or civil defense fire license is required. The tax office will issue the Business Registration Certificate within the statutory processing period after verifying the company name, address, representative, and business scope.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Registered office lease or proof of physical address
Identity card of the company representative
Business Registration application form
Articles of Incorporation and first board resolution
Employer registration forms for labor and health insurance
Digital webtoon platform agreements if required for tax classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Taxation Bureau delays the business registration, follow up by written request and provide proof of company registration; if a discrepancy in the business scope is identified, submit an amended scope application through the Department of Commerce before reapplying; if the business registration is rejected, file an appeal with the local tax authority or the Ministry of Finance within 30 days after the rejection is served.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration and National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; online integrated e-Tax portal at https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a locally incorporated Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, first complete company registration with the Department of Commerce of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and obtain the Company Registration Certificate. Within 15 calendar days of starting business, apply to the local National Taxation Bureau for business tax registration using the prescribed Business Tax Registration Application. Attach the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, representative identification, business premises proof, and board resolution. For a foreign non-resident enterprise with no fixed place of business selling electronic services to Taiwan consumers, a simplified cross-border electronic services tax registration must be submitted through the Ministry of Finance online platform, including the foreign company certificate, representative document, digital service description, and payment channel details. Upon approval, the National Taxation Bureau issues the entity's Tax Identification Number (TIN) and uniform invoice number series. For the Apple IAP and Google Play Billing payment rails, the Taiwan tax registration covers the local collection agent status if a domestic billing agent is used; otherwise the foreign seller must perform cross-border VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Taiwan's Income Tax Act imposes profit-seeking enterprise income tax at the entity level for a limited liability company and does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT, locally named Business Tax under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For domestic goods sellers, monthly taxable sales exceeding NT$80,000; for domestic service providers, monthly taxable sales exceeding NT$40,000; for foreign businesses without a fixed place of business selling electronic services to Taiwan individual consumers, annual taxable sales exceeding NT$480,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the issuance of Uniform Invoices. E-invoicing must use the Ministry of Finance integrated e-invoice platform, and eligible businesses integrate through the E-Invoice Turnkey API to upload invoice data. There is no real-time tax authority pre-clearance stamping for standard B2C cloud invoices, but cloud invoices carry anti-fraud QR codes and randomized check numbers, and transaction data is subject to fiscal retention and automated post-issue verification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, exported goods departing Taiwan customs territory and services provided for use outside Taiwan or in connection with exported goods qualify for zero-rated VAT. Digital webtoon subscriptions and multilingual chapter unlocking services sold to overseas readers qualify as service exports if the services are not consumed within Taiwan and the supplier retains evidence of foreign consumption, payment from abroad, and outward service jurisdiction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Form) issued by Customs Administration
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill or Combined Transport Document
Foreign exchange earnings certificate or Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC)
Digital service export contract and subscription plan documentation evidencing overseas consumers
Payment gateway settlement statements from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing identifying non-Taiwan user jurisdictions
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the exporter fails to retain or produce the required customs, logistics, invoice, and FX repatriation documentation, the tax authority may deny zero-rating and retroactively assess 5% VAT on the exported sales for up to seven years, with interest from the original due date. Penalties of up to five times the underpaid tax may be imposed for confirmed fraudulent zero-rating claims, and false foreign exchange declaration violations may trigger separate administrative fines under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC), Foreign Exchange Department
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan runs a managed-floating, market-clearing foreign exchange system. The New Taiwan dollar is freely convertible for current-account trade and service payments and for approved capital-account movements. A Taiwan-resident entity may receive, hold, and sell foreign currency without surrender to the state; conversion is carried out with designated foreign-exchange banks at quoted market rates. Remittances above the Central Bank's reporting threshold require a Foreign Exchange Transaction Report and, for direct-investment capital, a prior approval from the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Investment Commission. Profit distributions and royalty remittances must be supported by audited financial statements and withholding-tax certificates; the Taiwan-side convertibility hurdle is moderate, not license-based. The principal non-convertibility exposure in this CN/TW structure is on the mainland side: the Chinese JV shareholder must complete NDRC, MOFCOM and SAFE ODI registration before funding the Taiwan entity. Without that statutory evidence, the Taiwan bank will decline the inbound wire as a suspected capital-smuggling transaction. There are no domestic limitations on holding USD or repatriating declared dividends once tax clearance and beneficial-ownership certification are produced.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan imposes no mandatory surrender of export foreign-exchange earnings and no required conversion ratio to New Taiwan dollars. Export receipts can be retained in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account, offset against approved import payments, or sold to a designated bank at market rate. The bank that receives the settlement must verify the customs export declaration, the purchase order and the invoice; for a single settlement exceeding US$100,000, the Central Bank's Reporting System requires a Foreign Exchange Settlement/Declaration form completed by the company. For mandatory reporting, banks must file the transaction with the Central Bank on the standard schedule, normally by the fifth business day after the month of settlement. No statutory timeline requires the exporter to convert within a set number of days; the only filing deadline is the bank's monthly reporting cutoff.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: 1.5/10 - Not viable as a primary corporate treasury rail. Taiwan's Banking Act, Foreign Exchange Control Act and FSC licensing framework require any deposit-taking or foreign-exchange service to be provided by a licensed bank or a regulated offshore banking unit. Offshore digital EMIs are legally barred from opening a domestic Taiwan corporate account, issuing a local account number, or conducting B2B clearing on behalf of the JV. The only acceptable function is as a supplemental collection or billing conduit for consumer platforms such as Apple IAP or Google Play, with funds automatically swept to a licensed Tier-1 bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch appearance is mandatory. Taiwan banks require the statutory responsible person and authorised signatory directors to appear physically before a compliance officer to verify original IDs and witness the corporate seal and signature matrix. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for a newly incorporated JV with a mainland parent. A video interview can be used only to supplement, not replace, the mandatory in-person identity verification, and any foreign director who cannot appear must provide an apostilled board resolution authorising a local signing officer, yet the bank may still call that local officer to a branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex group structure with mainland multi-layer shareholders creates a money-laundering or UBO opacity risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Chinese business license, Taiwan JV incorporation registration, full shareholder register, notarised UBO declaration, group organisation chart identifying every controlling entity and natural person at or above 25%, passport/ID copies of UBOs, residence or visa evidence for the local director, and a Taiwanese attorney opinion confirming effective control and the absence of nominee shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Freshly capitalised JV receives a large first inward remittance from the mainland parent with only a generic digital-content purpose declared.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Sino-foreign joint venture agreement and MOEA Investment Commission approval letter; mainland ODI/FDI approval and SAFE foreign-exchange registration; bank-approved board resolution; CPA capital-verification instruction; route-of-funds statement showing each transfer leg; platform launch contracts and webtoon-content licence agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue model depends on Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, creating micro-payouts that do not match conventional trade invoices and can appear as unstructured source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple/Google developer agreements, 12-month payout statements, monetisation reports, breakdown by territory and content title, consumer refund/dispute registers, and a reconciliation schedule mapping each platform payout to the clearing account and filing base.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse-media or sanctions screening flags a cross-strait shareholder in creative-media licensing, creating IP-ownership and royalty ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening outputs from a recognised global compliance database, negative-news research with source timestamps, legal opinion on control and ownership, court/tax/customs clearance certificates for each UBO, webtoon copyright and trademark registration evidence, and a signed commitment to refresh KYC on material changes.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use the licensed Tier-1 Taiwanese bank as the receiving institution. The mainland parent must first complete its outbound ODI/SAFE filing and the Taiwan JV must finalise the MOEA foreign-investment approval. The parent sends a SWIFT MT103 from its mainland corporate account to the JV's dedicated capital-escrow account at Bank of Taiwan or Mega; the 70 tag must carry the JV registration case number and DIRECT INVESTMENT CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION reference; the Taiwanese bank will code the transaction under the Central Bank's direct-investment category in the foreign-exchange reporting system. For capital verification, the escrow funds must remain ring-fenced until a certified public accountant issues the capital verification certificate and the Ministry of Economic Affairs registration has been updated; the bank then releases funds to the operating TWD account. No alternative money-services business or EMI may be used for this capital injection leg.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for royalties, profit-sharing and licensed-content fees; Commercial Letters of Credit where purchase orders require title movement; and Documentary Collections for low-value recurring trade payments. For Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the JV should maintain a USD settlement account to receive platform payouts and then sweep those balances into the operating TWD account or use them for media-related MT103 payments. Outbound royalties to the mainland parent must attach the content licence agreement, withholding-tax summary and commercial invoice; isolated payments without title or production registration will be blocked by the bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/TWD forward contracts up to 24 months for hedging forecast platform receivables and royalty payables, provided the underlying exposures are supported by board-approved cash-flow projections.
Non-deliverable USD/TWD forwards executed with a licensed bank where the Central Bank requires proof of underlying commercial exposure and prohibits speculative open NDF positions.

Cross-currency swaps for matched long-term foreign-currency debt service only; the swap must be tied to a specific borrowing relationship and cannot be used for unlinked market-making or balance-sheet speculation.
FX swaps between USD and TWD for temporary liquidity conversion, limited to 12-month tenors and supported by verified capital or trade transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary shareholders' meeting: approval of operating report, financial statements, surplus distribution or loss recovery proposal, and confirmation of certified public accountant appointment when audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company and Commerce Administrative Office; meeting records and compliance evidence retained at registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year financial accounts, no later than 30 June; for an approved non-calendar fiscal year, within six months after fiscal year end; any extension must be obtained from MOEA before the original statutory deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the statutory ordinary meeting or to prepare the required statements are liable to fines up to NT$100,000 under Company Act Articles 170 and 228; continued noncompliance after MOEA order, with business cessation for six consecutive months, supports administrative strike-off under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of shareholders' meeting minutes and, where the mandatory audit threshold is met, the CPA-audited and attested financial statements plus directors' report with the corporate registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA Company and Commerce Administrative Office, with a filing copy to the National Taxation Bureau for tax-linked financial records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the ordinary shareholders' meeting approves the financial statements; with a 30 June meeting, the latest complete filing is 30 July of the same year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Resolutions that are required to be registered cannot be asserted against bona fide third parties under Company Act Article 12; continuing default after a rectification order exposes the company to fines up to NT$100,000 and can lead to administrative strike-off of company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise income tax annual return and final self-assessed tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, competent for the registered business address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 May through 31 May for the preceding calendar year or approved fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a late-filing surcharge and interest under Articles 108 and 112 of the Income Tax Act, with monthly interest currently at a Ministry of Finance announced rate of 1.5% on unpaid tax; failure to file after demand permits assessment on available evidence and a penalty of up to 100% of underpaid tax, and prolonged tax delinquency can trigger tax registration cancellation and business registration strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax statement and remittance summary for wages, dividends, royalties, and non-resident payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January after the close of the calendar year for annual withholding statement filing; non-resident dividend, royalty, and other taxable payment withholding must be remitted within 10 days of payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file correct withholding statements attracts statutory fines ranging from NT$1,500 to NT$15,000 per statement under Articles 88 and 106 of the Income Tax Act, plus monthly interest and unpaid-tax surcharges; persistent noncompliance can cause the tax authority to cancel tax registration and recommend administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-driven foreign investment and UBO confirmation report for share transfers, capital changes, and changes to directors or ultimate beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, with simultaneous registration amendment at the MOEA Company and Commerce Administrative Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 days after any share transfer, registered capital increase or decrease, or change in ultimate beneficial owner; in a no-event year, annual confirmation is embedded in the shareholders' meeting package delivered by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported foreign-invested share transfers may render the foreign investment approval ineffective for remittance and protection purposes, expose the entity to monetary penalties under the Foreign Investment Act, and support de-registration or administrative strike-off after an MOEA enforcement order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and reconciliation of register of members, register of directors and supervisors, register of charges and pledges, minute book, share transfer ledger, and UBO records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors and company secretary or registered agent; records available for inspection by MOEA and the National Taxation Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completion no later than 30 June each year, prior to the ordinary shareholders' meeting; share transfer entries must be recorded in the register of members within 15 days of transfer registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficient statutory registers, stale minute books, or refusal to allow statutory inspection are punishable by fines up to NT$50,000, and aggravated noncompliance after MOEA order can lead to administrative strike-off of the company registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Company Act Article 20 and MOEA and Financial Supervisory Commission gazettes, an independent certified public accountant audit is legally mandatory when any of the following quantitative triggers are met: (i) balance-sheet paid-in capital reaches NT$30,000,000 or more; (ii) annual gross turnover or operating revenue exceeds NT$100,000,000 for an enterprise operating under a financial-services, payment, or government-certified digital-content license requiring CPA-attested statements; or (iii) the entity employs 100 or more workers and is required by labor pension law to prepare actuarial or pension-fund financial statements reviewed by a certified public accountant or actuary. For the webtoon syndication entity, the ordinary legal audit trigger is therefore paid-in capital of NT$30,000,000 or more; a workforce above 100 employees triggers pension-fund audit obligations, while turnover alone does not mandate an audit for an unlisted private limited company unless an industry-specific FSC order or foreign-investment approval condition so requires.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TFRS), substantially converged with IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission, for companies above the regulatory size threshold; private small and medium-sized enterprises may apply the Business Entity Accounting Act and SME Financial Reporting Standards issued by the MOEA, with books and supporting vouchers maintained in New Taiwan Dollars in accordance with the approved fiscal year.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose a separate stand-alone annual UBO return; instead, the company must maintain current shareholder and ultimate beneficial ownership records and must file any share transfer, capital change, director change, or UBO change with the MOEA registration authority within the applicable event-driven window, which is 30 days for foreign-invested share transfer reporting to the Investment Commission and 15 days for share transfer entries in the register of members. As the annual checkpoint, the board and shareholders must confirm the registered shareholder list, share pledges, and ultimate beneficial ownership at the ordinary shareholders' meeting no later than 30 June, and the meeting minute must be retained with the statutory registers as evidence of the annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges, Pledges, and Mortgages
Share Transfer Ledger and Stock Certificate Records
General Ledger and Supporting Accounting Vouchers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year for registered office, corporate secretary and registered agent services, statutory mailing address handling, and compliance calendar administration in Taiwan
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 6,500 per year for a private Taiwan limited company with paid-in capital near or above the NT$30 million audit threshold; consolidated TFRS or IFRS group audits may range from USD 8,000 to USD 18,000 per year

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan does not offer a blanket corporate tax holiday. However, preferential treatments are available under the Statute for Industrial Innovation (investment tax credits up to 15% for R&D expenditures and 3% to 5% for certain qualified machinery/equipment investments), the Free Economic Pilot Zones Act (exemption or reduced corporate income tax on operating income derived from approved export-oriented logistics or digital-content activities), and the Small and Medium Enterprise Development Statute (a reduced rate of 20% on the first NT$120,000 of taxable income). In addition, eligible digital publishing companies may claim a 20% deduction from taxable income for certified digital-content development costs, bringing the effective tax rate below the 20% statutory headline rate for the incremental benefit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form 15) filed via the Ministry of Finance e-Filing Portal (Tax Data Gateway) or the IRS (Integrated Tax Return System) for income years beginning before or after 2025; electronically signed with a natural-person or corporate-certificate (X.509).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing must occur within five months after the fiscal year-end (for calendar-year enterprises, from 1 May to 31 May). Enterprises adopting a special fiscal year must file within five months after the close of that special fiscal year. An interim (provisional) corporate income tax payment is due on 31 August for the first half-year, equal to one-half of the prior year's assessed tax amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit-seeking enterprise registration: legally registered name, uniform customer number (Taiwan tax ID), registered address, date of incorporation, industry code (ISIC 9000 / NAICS 511130), and major shareholder ownership table.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Taiwan-resident JV name (CN_JV_LTD) and its Taiwan branch or head-office address. If the foreign (CN) parent holds a substantial equity interest, disclose the parent's name, address, and tax residency certificate number. Failure to disclose beneficial foreign ownership may trigger the anti-treaty-shopping audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: total global and Taiwan-source sales from Webtoon chapter unlocking, digital comic subscriptions, premium content purchases, advertising, and licensing royalties received from app stores (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the gross invoice value from Taiwan users and platform remittances before deduction of Apple/Google commission fees. If the JV is treated as the principal selling to Taiwanese consumers, the full consumer-paid price is gross revenue; the 15% to 30% platform commission is a deductible operating expense, not an income offset. Any amount passing through to foreign licensors under a distribution-only agency agreement must be excluded from revenue and shown as a liability payable to the foreign principal, with withholding tax applied on the licence fee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct content acquisition costs: author royalties, commissioned webtoon production costs, digital hosting costs, and rights licensing fees paid to PRC content providers or foreign studios.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only if supported by written contracts, documentary substance of the service, and proper withholding tax on cross-border remittances. Payments to non-residents for copyright licensing (comic/webtoon content) are subject to VAT and income tax withholding at the statutory 20% royalty WHT, unless a reduced treaty rate is claimed. The JV must maintain the Chinese parent's Tax Residency Certificate and a beneficial ownership declaration to apply the Cross-Strait Tax Arrangement (10% for royalties when beneficial owner is a direct shareholder or connected payer) — otherwise the full 20% is withheld and no deduction may be taken.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: employee salaries, marketing, server/cloud infrastructure, content development and R&D expenditure, administrative overhead, and legal fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim post-carryover investment tax credits for qualifying digital-content R&D (App/Webtoon platform software development). Use an employee time-allocation log to substantiate R&D activities in Taiwan. Disallow entertainment expenses in excess of statutory ceilings, and reject any intercompany fee paid to a related party without an arm's-length transfer pricing analysis. For payments to related parties outside Taiwan (especially PRC or Hong Kong entities), attach the China/Taiwan Master File/Local File disclosure schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before loss carryover: reconcile gross profit percentage and add non-operating income (interest, dividends, foreign exchange gain).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add foreign exchange gains from Apple/Google USD remittances and subtract forex losses only if realised. Any prior-year net operating loss (carried forward within ten years) must be supported by a certified audit and tax-loss carryforward register. Non-resident shareholders must ensure the JV correctly allocates income to Taiwan under Article 41 of the Income Tax Act; a simple 'paper allocation' to a lower-tax jurisdiction (e.g., using the CN parent as invoicing agent) is a fatal red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax: taxable income multiplied by the 20% statutory rate, offset by foreign tax credits, investment tax credits, and the basic tax differential under the AMT regime (minimum tax to be paid if regular tax is less than 12%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 20% rate. Foreign tax credits are limited to the Taiwan tax attributable to the foreign-source income and require certified tax returns from the source country. The AMT floor (12% of alternative minimum taxable income above the exemption) may apply when the JV is aggressively deductions or treaty-exempt. For a JV taxed as a resident company, the foreign parent is not subject to branch-profit remittance tax; instead, declared dividends to the PRC parent will be subject to the 21% WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Undistributed retained earnings (Post-2018): If profits have not been distributed to shareholders within the following year, an additional 5% tax is levied on undistributed surplus for non-SME enterprises unless reinvested in qualified equipment or R&D.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The JV should plan dividend payout before year-end to avoid the 5% retained earnings tax. For a PRC joint-venture shareholder, a distribution planned in accordance with the Tax Collection Act trigger the 21% WHT unless treaty relief is granted under the Cross-Strait Arrangement (10% on direct qualifying shareholding or 15% otherwise). Prepare board resolution documentation and the foreign shareholder's beneficial-ownership affidavit before the distribution date; otherwise, the JV will be assessed the WHT and the payment will be treated as constructive dividend to the PRC parent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Form 15 return triggers a surcharge of 3% of the understated tax for each month or fraction thereof, up to a maximum of 30% of the assessed tax amount; in addition, per-month interest accrues at the current Central Bank rediscount rate plus 2%. If the taxpayer files no return within the statutory period, the tax authority may assess the tax by estimation and impose a fine under Article 110 of the Tax Collection Act of not more than ten times the amount of tax under-assessed. For fraudulent evasion (intent to conceal income or falsify receipts), criminal referral under Article 41 of the Tax Evasion Act (the charge of non-payment of tax by unlawful means) can lead to a fine of up to NT$5,000,000 and imprisonment for up to five years if the tax evaded exceeds NT$500,000. Late or non-payment of withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties due to a non-resident renders the withholding agent personally liable for the unpaid WHT and a penalty equal to 20% (or twice) of the under-withheld tax if the failure is deliberate; criminal fraud charges are possible where the withheld amount is taken into the JV's own bank account and never remitted to the treasury.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on the gross amount of any dividend paid by a Taiwan resident enterprise to a non-resident shareholder (per Article 88 of the Income Tax Act, rate effective since 2018). For a profit-seeking enterprise resident in Taiwan (including a local JV), dividends distributed to another Taiwan resident entity are exempt and subject to an integrated tax regime with a 5% retained-earnings tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The PRC-Taiwan Cross-Strait Taxation Arrangement (upon effective enforcement) provides for a reduced dividend WHT of 10% for the beneficial owner that is a company holding at least 25% of the paying company's capital, and 15% in all other cases. To invoke treaty relief, the JV (as withholding agent) must: (1) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Chinese tax authority for the fiscal year of the payment; (2) obtain a signed beneficial-ownership declaration (Form D-10) from the PRC parent stating that the parent is not a conduit, has full right to the dividend, and meets the 25% shareholding period/maintenance requirement; (3) file a formal application for reduced withholding with the Taiwan National Taxation Bureau (income tax withholding section) before the remittance date; (4) provide certified Chinese business-registration and share-registration documents and audited financial statements demonstrating the parent's operational activity (CIGA) in China; (5) obtain an advance tax ruling or a written approval of the reduced rate if the amount exceeds a threshold set by the provincial tax office. The approval is normally issued within two weeks, but any payment made before approval is subject to the 21% WHT; a subsequent refund will only be granted after a review of the beneficial ownership substance and on the condition that the PRC parent is not a shell company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax rates for non-residents: royalties for the use of or right to use copyrighted content (webtoon/comic) 20% of the gross consideration; interest income 20% (15% for interest from a Taiwanese financial institution to a non-resident); and dividends 21%. Under the Cross-Strait Arrangement, royalties are generally reduced to 10% when the beneficial owner is a resident of the other side and the right is used in the other territory; interest is reduced to 10% (or 15% if the interest is paid on a loan from a financial institution). The same TRC, BO declaration, and pre-payment application procedures described above apply to the reduced rates. Failure to secure pre-approval or to correctly classify a payment as a royalty rather than a service fee can expose the payer to an additional 20% penalty and re-characterization of the payment as a constructive dividend (21% WHT) if the related party does not demonstrate real licensing substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NT$200,000,000 (approximately US$6.5 million) in aggregate cross-border related-party transactions in a fiscal year, or NT$100,000,000 (approximately US$3.3 million) in domestic related-party transactions, triggers mandatory preparation of a Transfer Pricing Local File and Master File (per the Assessment Rules on Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax and Transfer Pricing). A Taiwan subsidiary is also required to file a country-by-country report (CbCR) if its foreign parent group has group revenue exceeding NT$27 billion and the Taiwan entity alone books NT$50 million or more of related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute resembling OECD/Caribbean ESR. However, the Taiwan tax authority applies the double-rollover anti-avoidance rule under Article 43-4 of the Income Tax Act, the Controlled Foreign Corporation (CFC) rule (effective January 2023), and the 'place of actual management' (PAM) doctrine to recharacterize a Taiwan-registered entity as a non-resident if substantive decisions and CIGA (e.g., product development, contract negotiation, board meetings and R&D staff leadership) take place outside Taiwan, especially in mainland China. For ISIC 9000 (digital webtoon publishing), the CIGA are: (1) content acquisition, negotiation and licensing agreements; (2) digital platform development, server management, and customer support in Taiwan; and (3) strategic direction of app-store sales distributions. If the JV is a mere mailbox company receiving Apple/Google royalty flows and passing them to the PRC parent, the Taiwan tax authority will either (a) treat the JV as a non-resident enterprise and assess a 20% WHT on all Taiwan-source income, or (b) invoke the CFC rules to attribute the retained profits to the PRC parent for PRC tax purposes, while denying Taiwan-resident tax filing benefits. Therefore, the JV must maintain physical office space, at least one full-time Taiwan-resident senior manager, local board-meeting minutes, and a payroll schedule showing Taiwanese employees performing the core CIGA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional under-reporting of Webtoon chapter-unlocking revenue, specifically (a) excluding Apple/Google IAP remittances by routing sales through a PRC payment processor, (b) recognizing revenue only upon the foreign parent's invoice instead of the time of sale to Taiwanese users, or (c) fabricating a fictitious royalty expense to divert profits to a Hong Kong shell licensor without any economic substance, thereby reducing the Taiwan taxable income below the 12% AMT threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 110 of the Tax Collection Act: a fine of up to five times the amount of tax evaded; Article 41 of the Tax Evasion Act: criminal fine up to NT$5,000,000 and imprisonment for a term of not more than five years where tax is concealed through unlawful means. In addition, under Article 35 of the Business Tax Act, fraudulent VAT/income tax collection can lead to a fine of 100% to 300% of the evaded amount. The JV's tax return may be reassessed within a 7-year limitation period for factual errors and within 10 years for cases not filed at all (or fraudulent).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Non-resident (PRC/Taiwan) directors who sign misleading financial statements may be jointly and severally liable for the underpaid tax corpus, interest, and penalties. The court can issue an order to pierce the corporate veil where the director used the JV as a ‘mere instrumentality’ to evade tax, attaching personal assets of the directors. In addition, the National Taxation Bureau can apply for a travel-ban order against the directors under the Tax Collection Enforcement Act, preventing departure from Taiwan until the tax debt is settled. Criminal conviction for tax fraud carries up to five years' imprisonment plus a fine; professional directors may be disqualified from serving as officers of any Taiwanese company under the Company Act for ten years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance (CIGA Misdeclaration)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Taiwan JV is registered as a profit-seeking enterprise but has no office, no employees, no bank account in Taiwan, and its board of directors (all located in Shanghai) passes board resolutions without meeting in Taiwan. The JV's only operation is a series of pass-through contracts: Apple/Google pay the JV, the JV immediately wire-transfers 95% of the receipts to the PRC parent as 'content licensing fee', and the JV declares negligible profit. The actual CIGA (software development, user acquisition, sales strategy) is performed in Beijing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 10 of the Income Tax Act and the Board of Taxation's interpretative ruling on the ‘central place of management and control,’ the Taiwan tax authority may treat the JV as a non-resident enterprise and tax all Taiwan-source digital-content income at the 20% WHT rate (gross) without deductions. The false statement of residence and business activity triggers the anti-abuse provision of Article 43-4 (investment income attribution) and Article 43-1 (unreasonable related-party allocation) allowing the authority to disallow the cost and expense allocation and recharacterize the licensing fee as a constructive dividend. The Company Act imposes an administrative fine of NT$1,000,000 to NT$5,000,000 for filing false registration documents, and the Business Registration law may order the dissolution of the shell-company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly declare a shell company as a Taiwan resident operator are personally subject to piercing of the corporate veil, rendering their personal assets (including PRC-held properties) liable for corporate tax debt. The tax authority may further blacklist (list as a major conscientious delinquent) the director and the JV, causing a ban on luxury transactions and a freeze on all Taiwan bank accounts. Under the Money Laundering Control Act, if the shell company is used to pass funds through Apple/Google IAP for the benefit of undisclosed shareholders, the directors face criminal liability of up to two years' imprisonment, a fine of up to NT$5,000,000, and the forfeiture of the illicit pathway.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Withholding Tax Violations on Outbound Royalties/Interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The JV fails to prepare an arm's-length Transfer Pricing Local File despite the fact that its related-party transactions exceed NT$200,000,000 for the year (e.g., it pays NT$160,000,000 royalty to its PRC parent webtoon studio and NT$50,000,000 interest to its HK finance subsidiary). In addition, it remits the royalty without withholding any income tax (0%), claiming a mistaken 'treaty-free' status absent a TRC, and without issuing a withholding certificate to the payee. Alternatively, it structures the royalty as a 'management service fee' to avoid the 10% royalty WHT while providing no evidence of service substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act allows the tax authority to adjust the transaction back to arm's length; the adjustment triggers a shortfall tax rate of 20% plus a TP adjustment penalty of 100% of the understated tax under Article 110(1) of the Tax Collection Act. Failure to maintain TP documentation pursuant to the Assessment Rules is punishable by an administrative fine of up to NT$500,000. For the withholding violation, Articles 114-1 and 114-2 of the Income Tax Act impose a penalty of twice the amount that should have been withheld, but in any event not less than NT$10,000. If the non-resident payee has no TRC and the JV relies on the parent's claim of ‘license-free’, the entire payment is reclassified as a taxable distribution subject to the 21% WHT and the same penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: As the withholding agent, the JV's responsible director is personally liable for the full amount of the under-withheld 20% or 10% WHT and penalties if the JV's assets are insufficient. The tax authority can file a criminal complaint under Article 35 of the Tax Collection Act for failure to account for and pay tax withheld from another person, which is a felony carrying a criminal fine from NT$100,000 to NT$5,000,000 and imprisonment for up to five years. A director who issues a false beneficial-ownership declaration or who signs the intercompany contract knowing the royalty rate to be inflated (e.g., a 60% net margin to the PRC parent) will be jointly and severally liable for the entire TP adjustment amount. The director is also subject to a travel ban and admission to the tax delinquent blacklist until the debt is resolved.
